newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Brit Land eyes more jt ventures.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Brit Land eyes more jt ventures.

text.p: UK property group British Land will look for more joint venture opportunities following the success of recent link-ups with non-property groups, its finance director John Weston Smith said on Wednesday.

"I think there will be more (joint ventures), quite where and when I can't say, but they are something we will look to do," Weston Smith told Reuters after British Land had announced pre-tax profits of 91.2 million stg for 1996/97.
British Land likes to establish joint ventures with non-property groups, provides the property expertise, splits the venture 50/50 and raise separate finance.
It has already linked up with Scottish and Newcastle Plc , Great Universal Stores Plc and Tesco Plc .
Joint ventures means British Land does not use up its own credit, expands assets under management on which it can achieve growth, widens its spread and reduces risk and give it management fees.
"They have a lot of merits," Weston Smith said.
Weston Smith said the firm's London Corn Exchange development had been nearly completely let and what was not yet let was almost all under offer. But he declined to disclose the rent level achieved.
He said British Land expected to develop further vacant sites on Euston Road in central London but while he would not rule out a speculative development, he said this was less likely.
And the firm is waiting for a response to its application for planning permission for the redevelopment of the Plantation House site in the City of London.
British Land was recently named in a report as a possible bidder for rival MEPC but Weston Smith said such rumours were commonplace.

While there were possible mergers in the sector, such moves were always difficult, not only because of the complications involved in such deals but also when share prices were at a premium as they currently are, he added.

"We've been interested in share stakes from time to time, but corporate activity is pretty difficult to do unless you can get a very strong position. I don't see it as a line we are going to go along."
